text:

What we do, and how we do it

Six kinds of work. For each: what is included, who it suits, and how a project runs.

Websites

Marketing and brand sites you can edit yourself.

What’s included
Design and build in Next.js
A content system your team can edit without a developer
Performance and accessibility checks before launch
Structured data and technical SEO
Who it’s for

Teams that need a site that loads quickly, reads clearly and doesn’t need a developer for every change to the text.

How we work

We start from the page structure and your real content, design in the browser, and send a working preview link at the end of every two-week cycle.

Web apps and SaaS

Software people log into: accounts, data and the screens around them.

What’s included
Accounts, roles and permissions
Subscription billing with Stripe
Dashboards, reports and exports
Automated tests for the parts that must not break
Who it’s for

Founders and teams turning a process or a product idea into software that several people use every day.

How we work

We build the smallest version that proves the idea, put it in front of real users, and grow it from what we learn.

AI automation and assistants

Language-model tools for repetitive work, with a person checking the result.

What’s included
Extracting and sorting information from documents
Assistants that answer from your own documents and cite them
A review queue for anything uncertain
Tracking of accuracy, usage and cost
Who it’s for

Teams with repetitive, document-heavy work where a person still needs to approve the outcome.

How we work

We test against your own examples first and only automate the steps that hold up. Everything the system does is logged so it can be reviewed.

Integrations and backend

Dependable connections between your tools, and the services behind them.

What’s included
CRM sync with HubSpot, Salesforce or your own system
Payment and webhook handling that survives retries
APIs, queues and scheduled jobs
Database design in PostgreSQL
Who it’s for

Teams whose tools don’t talk to each other, or whose data has outgrown a spreadsheet.

How we work

We map what moves where before writing code, then build in small steps with tests, so each connection can be checked on its own.

Cloud and DevOps

Hosting, deployment and monitoring set up properly, in your own accounts.

What’s included
Infrastructure written as code
Automated deployment with preview links
Error tracking and alerts
Secrets in a managed vault, least-privilege access
Who it’s for

Teams who want releases to be routine and who need to own their infrastructure.

How we work

Everything is created under accounts you own, documented as we go, and handed over with a walkthrough.

Care and maintenance

Updates, fixes and small improvements after launch.

What’s included
Dependency updates and security patches
Uptime and error monitoring
A monthly block of time for improvements
A named person to contact
Who it’s for

Anyone who has launched something and doesn’t want it to quietly fall behind.

How we work

Terms, response times and what is covered are written into the proposal before work starts.

How a project runs

Four steps, in this order, on every engagement.

Scoping call

Thirty minutes on the problem, the constraints and the timeline. No preparation needed.

Written proposal

Fixed-scope milestones with a price for each, and a plain list of what is out of scope.

Two-week build cycles

Every cycle ends with a working preview link and a short review with the people writing the code.

Handover

Code, infrastructure accounts and documentation are yours. Ongoing support is optional.

How we handle security

What we do on every project, written plainly. Formal compliance such as SOC 2, HIPAA or PCI DSS needs its own audit; if you need one, we scope that work with you openly.

Work lives in your repository and services run in your cloud accounts from the first day.
Access is least-privilege and is removed when the engagement ends.
Secrets are kept in a managed vault, never in source code or chat.
Dependencies are audited on every release, with automated update checks.
Sign-in, input validation and rate limiting are reviewed against the OWASP Top 10 before launch.
Data is encrypted in transit, and at rest wherever the platform supports it.
A mutual NDA is available before you share anything sensitive.
Questions we’re asked
Who owns the code and the accounts?

You do. Work happens in your Git organisation and cloud services are set up under your own accounts. Nothing is licensed back to you, and there is no lock-in.

Privacy

This site collects very little. This page says exactly what, why, and how to have it removed.

Who we are

This website is run by OrbiTech. For privacy questions, write to [Privacy contact email].

What we collect

The contact form. When you send a message we receive the details you type: your name, email address and message, and, if you choose to give them, your company, project type, budget, timing and a budget estimate from the estimator. We use them to reply to you and to scope any work you ask about.

How the message reaches us. The form sends your message by email through Resend, an email delivery service. It is not stored in a database on this website.

Spam protection. To limit repeated submissions, the server briefly remembers your network address in memory for ten minutes. It is not written to disk or shared.

Server logs. Our hosting provider [Hosting provider] may keep standard request logs, such as your network address and browser type, for security and reliability.

What we don’t do

This site sets no cookies, runs no analytics or advertising trackers, and loads its fonts from its own server, so your browser makes no requests to font or analytics companies.

How long we keep it

We keep enquiries for [Retention period, e.g. 12 months], or until you ask us to delete them. If we work together, project records are kept as the contract says.

Your choices

You can ask what we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it, by emailing the address above. Depending on where you live, you may have further rights under local law.

Who we are

The contact form. When you send a message we receive the details you type: your name, email address and message, and, if you choose to give them, your company, project type, budget, timing and a budget estimate from the estimator. We use them to reply to you and to scope any work you ask about.

Spam protection. To limit repeated submissions, the server briefly remembers your network address in memory for ten minutes. It is not written to disk or shared.
